In PHP 8 the concatenation operator '.' has lower precedence than '+', so it evaluates as 'sum: ' . (2 + 3).

PHP converts the numeric string '5' to an integer, so '5' + 5 evaluates to 10.

str_contains() checks if the haystack contains the needle substring, and 'Hello world' contains 'world', so it returns true.
str_pad() can pad on the right (default), left, or both sides using the STR_PAD_* constants.
By default trim() strips all whitespace characters, including tabs, newlines, carriage returns, null bytes, and vertical tabs, not just spaces.

ucfirst() returns a new string with the first character uppercased; strings are passed by value and are not modified in place.
Heredoc syntax (<<<EOT) performs variable interpolation, while nowdoc syntax (<<<'EOT') treats the content literally without parsing variables.
The sort() function reindexes the array with new numeric keys, so it does not preserve key-to-value associations (unlike asort()).
PHP automatically casts string keys containing valid decimal integers to integer keys.
in_array() uses loose (==) comparison by default; strict comparison requires setting the third parameter to true.

By default, array_slice() reindexes numeric keys; setting the fourth parameter (preserve_keys) to true keeps the original keys.

The + union keeps left-hand values for duplicate keys ('a' => 1) and adds the unique key 'b', giving 2 elements.
PHP 8.1 added support for unpacking arrays with string keys using the spread operator in array literals.
Since PHP 8.1, named arguments can be combined with argument unpacking, e.g. foo(...$args, name: 'value') is valid.
Anonymous functions in PHP do not inherit outer scope variables unless imported explicitly via 'use' (or are globals/superglobals).
func_num_args() returns the number of arguments actually passed to the function, regardless of the declared parameter list.
PHP arrow functions (fn) allow only a single expression and cannot contain a body with multiple statements in curly braces.
Arrow functions automatically capture outer variables by value (at definition time), not by reference; only anonymous function closures can capture by reference explicitly with &.
Declaring a closure as static prevents it from automatically binding the current $this, so $this cannot be used inside it unless explicitly bound, which PHP disallows for static closures.
The closure captured $x by value at creation time, so the later change to $x doesn't affect it.
In weak typing mode, PHP coerces numeric strings like "5" to the declared int type.
Constructor property promotion was introduced in PHP 8.0.
The 'final' keyword prevents a method (or class) from being overridden or extended in subclasses.
A final method cannot be overridden by child classes in PHP.
Private properties are only accessible within the class that declares them, not in subclasses; protected or public visibility would be required.
Anonymous classes are named class@anonymous followed by a NUL byte, then the file path, line number, and a counter.
Private methods are not inherited, so a child class may declare a method with the same name and any visibility without violating LSP or triggering inheritance visibility restrictions.
__get() is called for inaccessible properties, which includes both non-existent properties and existing ones that are not accessible (e.g., private/protected from outside scope).
Modifying a readonly property after initialization throws an Error (specifically 'Cannot modify readonly property'), not a generic Exception.
Interfaces may declare constants, which are inherited by implementing classes.
The instanceof operator checks whether an object is an instance of a specified class or interface.
Since PHP 5.3 (and more fully since PHP 8.0 which allows static in abstract/interface signatures), interfaces can declare static methods that implementing classes must define.
instanceof also returns true if the object implements a given interface, not just for class inheritance.
PHP interface methods cannot have body/default implementations; that behavior belongs to traits or abstract classes.
PHP abstract methods may be declared public or protected (but not private).
cases() returns an array of all enum cases, and Foo defines three cases: A, B, and C.
PHP traits may define properties and methods, but declaring constants in a trait is not allowed and results in a fatal error.
In PHP 7+, both Exception and Error implement the Throwable interface.
TypeError extends Error, not Exception; both only share the Throwable interface, so catch (Exception) does not catch TypeError.
The @ operator only suppresses errors and warnings; exceptions (Throwables) are not suppressed and will still propagate.
intdiv() throws a DivisionByZeroError when the divisor is zero.
The finally block always runs after try, regardless of whether an exception was thrown or caught.
An exception thrown in a finally block overrides any pending return value or exception from the try/catch blocks, directly affecting the result.
Any object, including an Exception instance, casts to boolean true.
Shutdown functions registered with register_shutdown_function() execute when script execution stops, including when exit() or die() is called.
The use statement only creates an alias; the class file is loaded later via autoloading when the class is actually referenced.
In PHP, `use function` imports a function, while `use const` imports a constant.
The App\ prefix is stripped and replaced by src/, so App\Controller\Api\UserController maps to src/Controller/Api/UserController.php.
Composer's generated autoloader registers its class-loading functions using spl_autoload_register(), making vendor/autoload.php include them in the SPL autoload queue.
__NAMESPACE__ returns the name of the current namespace (an empty string at the global level).
An unqualified class name in `new` is resolved relative to the current namespace (import rules apply), not from the global root.
PSR-4 replaces the namespace prefix 'App\' with the base directory 'src/', so App\Model\User maps to src/Model/User.php.
The use statement for importing namespaces must appear at file or namespace scope (top level), not inside a function, so imports cannot be scoped to a single function.
In PHP, arrays (like scalars) are assigned by value with copy-on-write semantics, unlike objects which are passed by handle/reference.
PHP arrays are assigned by value, so appending to $b does not modify $a, which still has 2 elements.
PHP functions have their own local scope, so global variables must be explicitly imported with the global keyword, the $GLOBALS array, or parameters.
unset($GLOBALS['x']) removes the global variable entirely from global scope, not just within the function.
The parameter is passed by reference (&$x), so incrementing $x inside the function modifies $n directly, yielding 6.
When iterating by value, foreach works on a copy of the array, so modifications made inside the loop are not reflected in the current iteration.
Static properties belong to the class itself, shared across all instances, so changes are visible to every object.
PHP casts boolean array keys to integers, so true becomes the integer key 1.
Since PHP 7, a generator can return a value via return, which is retrievable by calling $gen->getReturn() after the generator finishes.
Generators are forward-only; calling rewind() after iteration has started (including when fully consumed) throws an Exception.
yield from delegates iteration to another generator, Traversable, or array, aggregating its yielded values and return value.
Calling a generator function returns a Generator object, so get_class() returns 'Generator'.
The generator yields three values (1, 2, 3), so iterator_to_array produces an array with 3 elements, which count() reports.
SplStack implements a LIFO (last-in, first-out) stack, not a FIFO queue.
ArrayIterator wraps an array or object and lets you iterate over it using the Iterator interface.
ArrayObject implements IteratorAggregate, so its instances can be traversed with foreach.
password_hash() uses crypt() internally to generate a secure random salt automatically, and the salt option has been deprecated/ignored since PHP 7.
PASSWORD_DEFAULT currently points to bcrypt (via password_hash), not md5, and md5 is not a secure password hashing algorithm.
password_verify returns true because the hash was generated from the same 'secret' password using a cryptographically secure hash.
strip_tags() only removes HTML and PHP tags from a string and does not sanitize SQL; SQL injection should be prevented with prepared statements or proper escaping functions.
Calling session_regenerate_id() at login generates a new session ID, preventing attackers from using a known pre-assigned ID (session fixation).
php_sapi_name() returns a string describing the Server API type, such as 'cli' or 'fpm-fcgi'.
session_destroy() removes the session data stored on the server, but the client-side session cookie must be cleared separately, e.g. with setcookie().
PHP only populates $_SESSION after session_start() is called (or session.auto_start is enabled).
array_find() was added in PHP 8.4 as part of new array search functions.
Property hooks (get/set defined directly in property declarations) were introduced in PHP 8.4.
PHP 8.4 introduced asymmetric visibility with the `public private(set)` syntax for independent read/write scope on properties.
The #[\NoDiscard] attribute, which marks functions whose return values should not be ignored, was introduced in PHP 8.5.
The pipe operator |> was accepted via RFC and first shipped in PHP 8.5.
The clone($obj, ['x' => 1]) syntax with with-initializer arguments was introduced in PHP 8.4.
The array_first() and array_last() helper functions were introduced in PHP 8.4.
The Partial Function Application v2 RFC was accepted and implemented in PHP 8.5.
The clamp_v2 RFC proposing a clamp() function was rejected and never implemented in any PHP version.
The Context Managers RFC (inspired by Python's with statement) has not been adopted into PHP; it remains in draft/under discussion, not part of any released PHP version.
The Bound-Erased Generic Types RFC was declined in 2021, not 2026.
No RFC making thread-safe (ZTS) builds the PHP default has been accepted; ZTS remains an optional build-time configuration.
As of PHP 8.5, generics/parameterized types have not been implemented; PHP still lacks native generics support.
PHP 8.5 was released in November 2025 and remains the latest stable version, while PHP 8.6 is not yet released as of November 7, 2026.
The PHP 6 project (planned full Unicode support) was abandoned, so releases went directly from PHP 5.6 to PHP 7.0.
The #[\Deprecated] attribute RFC was accepted and implemented in PHP 8.4.
In clean/onion architecture, dependencies only point inward, so inner layers (domain) have no knowledge of outer layers (infrastructure, UI).
In a clean/decoupled architecture, domain entities depend only on PHP itself (and possibly the standard library), keeping them independent of Doctrine, Symfony, or any framework.

Controllers and Twig templates belong to the delivery/presentation (UI) layer; controllers merely trigger use cases, while the business logic itself resides in the use cases (application layer) and domain.
In onion architecture, the innermost layer is the domain model, with all other layers depending inward toward it.
Tools like deptrac statically analyze dependencies and fail the build when a layer calls another layer in a forbidden way.
Use cases should depend on domain-level input (DTOs/requests of plain data), not framework objects like HTTP requests or an EntityManager, to remain decoupled from delivery and infrastructure layers.
A repository provides a collection-like interface over aggregates/entities while encapsulating the underlying storage mechanism.
In clean architecture, database access belongs to the outer infrastructure layer, so swapping the database does not affect the inner domain and use-case layers.
An aggregate is a DDD concept: a cluster of domain objects treated as a single consistency unit with one root entity, not merely a database table.
A Value Object is defined by being immutable and compared by the equality of its field values rather than object identity.
In Domain-Driven Design, the aggregate root is the single external entry point through which all changes to an aggregate must pass.
In Domain-Driven Design, repositories are defined per aggregate root, since only roots can be retrieved and persisted directly.
In Domain-Driven Design, ubiquitous language is the shared vocabulary used consistently by developers and domain experts, and it directly shapes the model.
The universe of discourse is the boundary of shared context within which a model and its language are interpreted consistently, while outside it the same words may refer to other things.
DDD recommends rich domain models with behavior and invariants inside the entities, not anemic models with logic in transaction-script services.
In Domain-Driven Design, a bounded context defines the boundary within which a particular model applies, so the same concept (e.g., 'Customer') is represented by a separate class in each context.
Symfony services are lazily instantiated by default, being created only when first retrieved from the container.
The Symfony command `php bin/console debug:router` lists all registered routes.
Symfony's autowiring automatically detects and injects services based on type hints, so most services don't need manual declaration.
Twig compiles each template into a PHP class and stores the compiled code in a cache so it doesn't need to be recompiled on subsequent requests.
In dev, Symfony serializes the container and only recompiles it when a tracked resource (config, classes, etc.) changes, otherwise reusing the cached container.
Symfony uses the APP_ENV environment variable (set in .env) to select the active environment such as dev or prod.
Symfony must call the method from outside the class via the container, so the action method must be public (the class/service itself can be private, but not the method).
In Symfony's event dispatcher, subscribers and listeners are ordered solely by their priority values, not by the type of registration, so subscribers do not automatically run before listeners.
Symfony 6.0 removed the guard authenticator system in favor of the new authenticator-based security system introduced in 5.1.
Symfony's #[IsGranted] attribute enforces role/permission checks on controller methods, returning a 403 when access is denied.
Symfony voters are indeed the mechanism used to decide access to specific objects, checked via $this->isGranted('EDIT', $post) or the authorization checker.
Symfony 7 requires PHP 8.2+ and has removed support for doctrine annotations, so validation constraints must be declared as PHP attributes like #[Assert\NotBlank].
Symfony forms include CSRF protection by default, automatically adding and validating a CSRF token on submission.
Symfony validation always runs on the server when the form is submitted, regardless of any client-side HTML5 validation that passed.
Symfony's `make:form` command generates a new form class (FormType).
Symfony stores the security token in the session with the password already encoded (hashed), never in plain text.
Symfony stores configuration for each bundle (or topic like framework, twig, doctrine) in separate files under config/packages/.
In Symfony, the .env file is committed with safe dev defaults, while real secrets belong in .env.local, which is excluded from version control.
The `php bin/console debug:container` command lists all registered services and their aliases in the Symfony service container.
The compiled (dumped) Symfony service container is frozen at runtime, so calling setParameter() from a controller throws a LogicException.
Since Symfony 4.0, services are private by default and can only be accessed via dependency injection, not fetched directly from the container.
Bundles work without any configuration; config files in config/packages are only needed to customize a bundle's default settings.
In Symfony's services.yaml, environment variables are injected into parameters or service arguments using the %env(VAR)% syntax.
Symfony uses the APP_DEBUG environment variable (typically set to 1) to enable debug mode, which activates the profiler and Twig debugging.
Symfony Messenger allows a message to be handled by multiple handlers; you can register several handlers for the same message class.
The sync transport handles the message immediately inline (synchronously) rather than queuing it for a worker like the async transport does.
The Symfony Messenger worker is started with the `php bin/console messenger:consume` console command.
In Symfony Messenger, the retry_strategy option is defined inside each transport's configuration in messenger.yaml, so retries are configured per transport.
Symfony Messenger's default serializer encodes message bodies in JSON format.
The Symfony Scheduler component generates scheduled messages that are dispatched through the Messenger component for handling.
The built-in 'doctrine' Messenger transport stores queued messages in a doctrine_transport_messages database table via the Doctrine DBAL.

Symfony Messenger allows adding custom middleware via the messenger.bus configuration (getHandlerDecorators), and these can be ordered before or after the built-in middleware like SendMessageMiddleware and HandleMessageMiddleware.
Symfony follows a predictable schedule: new major versions every two years and new minor versions every six months, released in May and November.
Symfony 8 (the upcoming major release following Symfony 7) raises the minimum PHP requirement to 8.4.
Symfony 7.0 removed support for docblock-based annotations, requiring native PHP 8 attributes instead for validation, routes, and other metadata.
AssetMapper (introduced in Symfony 6.4) manages CSS/JS assets and JavaScript importmaps natively via importmap.php, without requiring Node.js or webpack.
Symfony 6.4 is a Long-Term Support (LTS) release, supported with bug fixes until November 2026 and security fixes until November 2027.
In Symfony, features marked as deprecated are removed in the next major version, so major releases do remove the previous branch's deprecations.
Because Symfony follows SemVer with backward compatibility breaks allowed in minor releases, UPGRADE guides are published with minor (and LTS) releases rather than every major release.
The symfony/asset-mapper component manages CSS/JS assets and the JavaScript importmap directly, without Node.js or Webpack.
Symfony x.2 versions are released at the end of November, so 8.2 was not yet out on 2026-11-07.
Symfony releases a new minor version every six months, and since 8.1 was released in May 2026, 8.2 follows in November 2026.
Symfony follows semver with minor releases every six months, so 8.1 (May 2026) is followed by 8.2 in November 2026.

Symfony 8.2 does not exist (current releases are in the 6.x/7.x line), and even real Symfony minor releases like x.2 never require application rewrites since backward compatibility is maintained within a major version.
PHP preserves backward compatibility within a major branch, so moving between minor versions like 8.1 to 8.2 should not require code changes.
Symfony follows the pattern of x.0 through x.4 minor releases per major branch, so the last minor version of the 8.x branch before Symfony 9.0 is 8.4.
Symfony's PHP requirements are fixed within a major version series, and Symfony 8.0 targets PHP 8.3, so 8.2 would not suddenly require PHP 8.5.
Symfony's deprecation policy guarantees that anything deprecated during the 8.x releases remains functional and is only removed in the next major version, 9.0.
Twig templates are sandboxed and cannot call arbitrary PHP functions; only whitelisted functions, filters, and methods are accessible.
Twig's default configuration enables autoescaping (with the 'html' strategy) for printed variables.
The Twig |e filter escapes a string for safe output, defaulting to the HTML context.
The twig/intl-extra extension provides the format_number filter, which formats a number according to the given locale.
In Twig, the |raw filter marks a value as safe, so auto-escaping is not applied to it.
In Twig, {{ }} outputs the value of an expression, while {% %} is used for control tags such as if, for, and set.
Twig allows declaring variables inside templates using the {% set %} tag.
The Twig dump() function outputs the debug structure of a variable when the debug extension is enabled.
Bootstrap provides ready-made CSS and JavaScript UI components; it is not a single-page application framework like Angular, React, or Vue.
The .container class is responsive and has a fixed max-width at each breakpoint, unlike .container-fluid which spans full width.
The Bootstrap grid splits each row into 12 columns, not 16.
Bootstrap defines six breakpoints, but xs (the smallest) has no infix, so the five infixes used in class names are sm, md, lg, xl, and xxl.
In Bootstrap-style utility classes like .mt-3 or .px-2, the numeric value is multiplied by the $spacer variable (default 1rem) to compute the spacing.
Bootstrap 5 components are enabled via data-bs-toggle (e.g. data-bs-toggle="dropdown"), replacing Bootstrap 4's data-toggle.
Bootstrap 5 removed the jQuery dependency, so its components are written in and work with plain vanilla JavaScript.
Bootstrap 5.3 enables dark mode with the data-bs-theme="dark" attribute on the html (or any) element, not a .dark class.
Doctrine does not create tables automatically at runtime; schema must be created explicitly via migration tools or SchemaTool commands.
EntityManager::persist() schedules a new entity for management, with INSERT SQL deferred until flush() is called.
EntityManager::merge() was removed in Doctrine ORM 3 as part of the cleanup of deprecated APIs.

DQL (Doctrine Query Language) is an object-oriented query language that operates on entities, their relationships, and fields, which Doctrine then translates into SQL over database tables and columns.
Doctrine's repository find() method returns null when no entity matches the given id.
DoctrineBundle does not automatically call flush(); you must call it explicitly on the EntityManager to persist changes, otherwise pending changes are discarded.
Once an entity is managed, the Unit of Work computes changesets at flush(), so persist() is only needed for new entities.
In Doctrine, remove() only marks the entity for deletion; the DELETE query is executed when flush() is called.
MVCC in PostgreSQL allows readers and writers to work concurrently without blocking each other.
The EXPLAIN command (e.g., `EXPLAIN SELECT ...`) shows the query execution plan without actually running the query.

While similar, SERIAL (creating a sequence-backed DEFAULT) and GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY (the SQL-standard identity column) differ in details, e.g. identity columns enforce stricter rules and use OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE for explicit inserts.
By default, PostgreSQL treats NULL values as distinct from each other, so a UNIQUE column can contain multiple NULLs (unlike SQL standard defaults in some other databases).
PostgreSQL provides the string_agg(value, separator) aggregate function to concatenate strings with a separator.
Plain VACUUM only marks dead tuple space as reusable within the table files; only VACUUM FULL rewrites the table and returns space to the operating system.
The PARTITION BY clause in a window function's OVER() definition divides rows into groups that the function is computed over independently.
READ COMMITTED only prevents dirty reads; it still allows non-repeatable reads and phantom reads within a transaction.
Without an explicit BEGIN, PostgreSQL executes each individual statement in its own implicit transaction, committing it immediately (autocommit behavior).
The COMMIT command ends a transaction and permanently saves all its changes.
Indexes help the WHERE clause of UPDATE and DELETE statements locate rows quickly, not just SELECT queries.
PostgreSQL supports SAVEPOINT to roll back part of a transaction without aborting the whole transaction.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually executes the query and shows real timings; plain EXPLAIN shows the plan without executing it.
The pgvector extension provides vector data types and similarity search indexes for storing and querying embeddings in PostgreSQL.
A partial index only indexes rows that satisfy its WHERE condition, making it smaller and faster for queries matching that condition.

PostgreSQL implements SERIALIZABLE via Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI), using snapshot isolation plus predicate locks to detect serialization conflicts, not by locking the rows a transaction reads.
HTTP status code 201 (Created) indicates the request succeeded and a new resource was created.
HTTP 204 No Content indicates a successful request with an empty response body.
DELETE is idempotent because repeating it on an already-deleted (or same) resource yields the same end state without additional side effects.
Access-Control-Allow-Origin is sent by the server in its response to indicate which origins are permitted, not by the client.
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests is specifically used when a client has sent too many requests in a given amount of time, i.e., exceeded a rate limit.
It's reversed: 4xx codes indicate client errors while 5xx codes indicate server-side errors.
The Content-Type header specifies the MIME type of the body in both HTTP requests and responses.
RFC 5789 explicitly states that PATCH responses are not required to be idempotent, unlike PUT which is required to be idempotent.
Plain == comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks and doesn't handle modern password hashing (like bcrypt's salted, variable output); you should use password_verify() or hash_equals().
CSRF tokens are generated server-side, stored in the session, included in forms, and verified on the server for unsafe requests like POST.
The Content-Security-Policy HTTP response header is used to deliver CSP directives to the browser.
OAuth 2.0 is an authorization (delegation) framework, not an authentication protocol; access tokens grant permissions and do not identify the user (that's OpenID Connect's role).
XSS is prevented by escaping/encoding output when displaying data, not merely by validating input before storing it in the database.
The authorization server returns an authorization code as the 'code' parameter to the redirect_uri, which is then exchanged for an access token.
Refresh tokens are long-lived credentials used to obtain new access tokens without requiring the user to re-authenticate.
A salt does not need to be secret; it is typically stored alongside the hash and is used during verification to defend against precomputed (rainbow table) attacks, not to hide the hash.
PHPUnit only discovers and runs test methods in classes that extend PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase.
setUp() runs before each individual test method; setUpBeforeClass() is the method that runs once before all tests in the class.
A PHPUnit data provider can return many sets of arguments, and the test runs once per set.
In PHPUnit, $this->expectException(ExceptionClass::class) declares that the tested code must throw an exception of the given class.
It's the reverse: mocks verify which methods were called, while stubs simply return canned data.
PHPUnit 10 introduced native PHP attributes like #[DataProvider], deprecating the @dataProvider annotation in favor of the attribute-based metadata API.
PHPUnit supports test dependencies via the @depends annotation, allowing a test to receive the return value of a test it depends on.
PHPUnit runs tests in random order when you pass --order-by=random (the older --random-order flag was removed in PHPUnit 8).
